text:
alex_ae: FYI — RetailCo (global retail chain) wants a POC followed by a 12mo dedicated commit. They asked for a 35% off list for the commit. Can we approve or counter?

maria_dealdesk: thanks for the heads up. do we have expected ARR and target MRR retention post-POC? need that for discount banding.

alex_ae: POC would be $55k ARR (3 months of dedicated + support) converting to $660k ARR annualized if they convert to full 12mo. they commit to a 12mo reserved pool after success; also want data-residency + SOC2 addendum.

jeff_finance: 35% is outside standard playbook for that ARR tier. our typical commit discount for 12mo at that scale is 20–25% depending on payment terms. what's their payment cadence?

alex_ae: they want quarterly billing. can do upfront annual if needed, but exec sponsor prefers quarterly.

nina_sales_ops: if we require annual upfront we can push discount to 30% but need finance signoff. also call out that dedicated pool adds operational cost — include a baseline infra allocation line item.

maria_dealdesk: propose counter: 25% with quarterly, 30% with annual upfront + 1% revenue-share credit if they hit >120% usage vs committed GPU hours. include a 90-day canary rollback clause.

sam_csm: also request that success criteria for POC are written into SOW: latency < 120ms p95 on key routes, 75% token-cost reduction vs baseline via batching. Otherwise hard to justify the reserved commit.

karina_legal: simple note — SOC2 + data residency addendum will add negotiation time. also need to confirm we can include the rollback (auto-fallback to hosted API) language without opening indemnity. I'll draft the minimal addendum.

jeff_finance: financials: with 25% discount ARR ~495k, margin still acceptable if we require 50% upfront credit on infra ramp for first month. if they insist on quarterly, ask for a 2% higher price or commit to shorter auto-renew.

alex_ae: customer likely balks at upfront. exec says they need flexibility. can we accept 27.5% as middle ground with quarterly + 60-day payment terms?

maria_dealdesk: 27.5% is unusual but can be approved if legal signs the rollback and finance takes the 60-day terms. @jeff_finance are you good to greenlight at 27.5% with those constraints?

jeff_finance: I can sign off on 27.5% only if we: (1) add a 6-month minimum termination notice post-conversion, (2) require a usage overage rate that's clearly documented, and (3) put a $50k ramp holdback tied to delivery milestones.

karina_legal: will draft the termination notice + overage clause. keep it tight so we don't leave open-ended credits.

alex_ae: ok i'll relay to RetailCo. ask: can dealdesk prep a pricing doc and SOW template I can send today?

nina_sales_ops: attaching quick proposal template in thread: https://internal.redwood/proposals/retailco-template (placeholder). I'll populate with two options: (A) quarterly + 27.5% (B) annual upfront + 30%.

dealbot: Note: routing to exec-approval queue for any discount >25%. Added ticket #DD-2026 to track.

maria_dealdesk: thanks — I'll pull the exec approval once legal drafts the addendum. please mark the POC success metrics in the SOW. if RetailCo accepts option B we can accelerate. :thumbsup:

alex_ae: perfect — i'll update customer and aim to get a signed LOI by end of week. will post back with their reaction.

sam_csm: +1 on documented success criteria. CSM will run post-POC handoff plan.

maria_dealdesk: leaving this open until exec sign-off. tagging @jeff_finance @karina_legal for follow-ups.
